glosses: to announce
давать (дать) анонс, объявление о предстоящем событии
To give public notice of, especially for the first time; to make known.

examples.text: Her [Queen Elizabeth’s] arrival was announced through the country by a peal of cannon from the ramparts.
Soon after the arrival of Mrs. Campbell, dinner was announced by Abboye. He came into the drawing room resplendent in his gold-and-white turban. […] His cummerbund matched the turban in gold lines.

The solitary, lumbering trolls of Scandinavian mythology would sometimes be turned to stone by exposure to sunlight. Barack Obama is hoping that several measures announced on June 4th will have a similarly paralysing effect on their modern incarnation, the patent troll.

glosses: To pronounce; to declare by judicial sentence.

examples.text: Publish laws, announce / Or life or death.

glosses: To act as announcer for (an event, usually sports).

examples.text: Our coach has retired, but occasionally he still announces the games.

glosses: To act or work as an announcer.

examples.text: Our coach has retired, but occasionally he still announces.

glosses: To follow behind (someone or something); to tail (someone or something).

examples.text: The hunters trailed their prey deep into the woods.

glosses: To drag (something) behind on the ground.

examples.text: You'll get your coat all muddy if you trail it around like that.
Our little life is but a gust That bends the branches of thy tree, And trails its blossoms in the dust!
"I saw your brother—I saw your brother," he said, nodding his head, as Archer lagged past him, trailing his spade, and scowling at the old gentleman in spectacles.

glosses: To leave (a trail of).

examples.text: He walked into the house, soaking wet, and trailed water all over the place.

glosses: To show a trailer of (a film, TV show etc.); to release or publish a preview of (a report etc.) in advance of the full publication.

examples.text: His new film was trailed on TV last night.
There were no surprises in this morning's much-trailed budget statement.

glosses: To hang or drag loosely behind; to move with a slow sweeping motion.

examples.text: The bride's long dress trailed behind her as she walked down the aisle.

Even now I behold a sign, A threatening of wrath divine, A watery, wandering star, through whose streaming hair, and the white Unfolding garments of light, That trail behind it afar, The constellations shine!

Cumberland sausage is about half as thick as your wrist and extends in a single rope several feet long, so that Mistrootchinson [Mister Hutchinson, the butcher], having weighed you one end while the other trailed over the edge of the scale, would then cut it for you like a draper selling a length of tape.

glosses: To run or climb like certain plants.

examples.text: The flowers glowed red and golden: snapdragons and sunflowers, and nasturtians trailing all over the turf walls and peeping in at the round windows.

glosses: To drag oneself lazily or reluctantly along.

examples.text: Our parents marched to church and we trailed behind.

glosses: To be losing, to be behind in a competition.

examples.text: Neil Lennon and his players have, in almost no time at all, roared back from trailing Rangers by 15 points in November to ending the year two points clear.

glosses: To carry (a firearm) with the breech near the ground and the upper part inclined forward, the piece being held by the right hand near the middle.
To create a trail in.

examples.text: The sun shone on burnished bodies and arm-bands, and robes of beaver trailed the grass as majestic fellows trod back and forth in the passion of eloquence.

[…] was no mean judge of racing and, having a suspicion of the possible result, she secreted a lemon in the commodious recesses of a dress which, while the height of fashion in those times, nevertheless trailed the grass.

In my mind's eye, I looked down at the toes of high-topped, lace-up leather boots, peeking from under a long brown skirt that bent the grass sideways as it trailed the ground and tented gently outward with every step.

glosses: To travel by following or creating trails.

examples.text: Trailed three miles down the North side and encamped early, making thirteen miles trailed to-day.

That control became visible each spring when they trailed back out of the low country to summer range.

glosses: To transport (livestock) by herding it along a trail.

examples.text: One operator on the Boise Forest in Idaho reports that where he formerly marketed 80-pound lambs after trailing them 10 days from the allotment, his lambs now often tip the scales at 100 pounds or better, mainly because only one day is required to transport an entire shipment to the railroad through the use of truck pullmans.
Genesis, the first book of the Holy Bible, relates the earliest known instance of cattle being trailed to better grass lands (unless Noah's trip with the ark is one).

In all areas where trails are present, stock must remain on the trails. Free trailing or loose herding is not permitted.

glosses: To take advantage of the ignorance of; to impose upon.

examples.text: I presently perceived she was (what is vernacularly termed) trailing Mrs. Dent; that is, playing on her ignorance.

glosses: The track or indication marking the route followed by something that has passed, such as the footprints of animal on land or the contrail of an airplane in the sky.

glosses: A route for travel over land, especially a narrow, unpaved pathway for use by hikers, horseback riders, etc.
A route or circuit generally.

examples.text: Politicians are on the campaign trail in preparation for this year's election.

glosses: A trailer broadcast on television for a forthcoming film or programme.

glosses: Faire connaître.

examples.text: Ce jeune gentilhomme, comme l’avait annoncé l’amiral, entrait à Paris par la porte Saint-Marcel vers la fin de la journée du 24 août 1572.
Les portières sont refermées, après la visite du contrôleur. Un dernier coup de sifflet annonce que le train va se mettre en marche…
Je quitte le lieutenant licencié et regagne le couvent, où la sœur converse m’annonce qu’un ami est venu me demander.
Bush l’avait annoncé depuis longtemps : il partirait en guerre quand bien même devrait-il être tout seul.
« Singulière affaire, assurément », se disait-elle. Elle en fut si bouleversée qu'elle ne devait même pas s’apercevoir que le coq avait déjà annoncé l'aube et que l'Orient peu à peu s'éclairait.

glosses: Faire connaitre son arrivée ou sa venue.
target_senses.note: Se dit particulièrement lorsqu’on prévient de l’arrivée d’une personne qui demande à entrer

examples.text: Le domestique annonça monsieur un tel. — Il fut très étonné lorsqu’on m’annonça.

— Veuillez m’annoncer à madame Donis, dit-il.
— Madame est dans le petit salon.
— Demandez si elle peut me recevoir.
En arrivant à Normée le berger souffle dans sa corne pour annoncer son retour. Les chiens aboient.

glosses: Faire connaître au public par une annonce.

examples.text: L’idée de déployer tous les fastes de la République et d’afficher une solennité churchillienne pour annoncer une augmentation de 1,6 point de la TVA ne peut venir que de cerveaux hallucinés.
Le titreur de Paris-Jour, ce matin, ne s'est pas embarrassé de nuances. Il a annoncé sur la largeur de la « une » : « Peyrefitte va interdire les minijupes. »

On les retrouve au kébab du coin, au bout de l'avenue Jean-Jaurès où une pancarte annonce : « Dernier kébab avant le périph », au Café de la musique du parc de la Villette, au café MK2 du quai de Seine.
— Ainsi le comprenait l’orateur qui flétrissait, il y a trois ans, dans un premier discours, ceux qu'on appelle des vendus, et qui s'annonçait déjà comme l’exécuteur des épurations nécessaires.

glosses: Prédire ; assurer qu’une chose arrivera.

examples.text: Les prophètes ont annoncé la venue du Messie. Un ange annonça à la Vierge le mystère de l’Incarnation.

glosses: Faire pressentir ce qui doit arriver.

examples.text: Le baromètre annonce le beau temps. La seconde scène de cette comédie en annonce le dénouement.

examples.text: M. de Vaize annonçait une cinquantaine d’années, il était grand et assez bien fait.

examples.text: L'été s’annonçait assez beau, bien qu'il crachinât de temps à autre sur la frange en bordure de mer.
